chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Who Dizzy Gillespie heard: Mangual, Vidal and Chano Pozo
summary: Machito says Dizzy never heard Bilingue; Chano Pozo impressed because he played between bass and drum without conflict.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So what is it that Dizzy Gillespie heard? I thought it was Bilingue at first. Now you are saying is Vidal that he heard and he wanted a conga drum player?
Before, Bilingue played with us about a couple of months. I don't think Dizzy Gillespie never heard Bilingue.
So who was it that he heard then, that he wanted?, the same thing.
Ahh - he never went to the Beachcomber for anything because in those days he was working with Calloway or he was traveling someplace else. The guy that he listened to was Mangual.

Jose Mangual, and Vidal, but he didn't get impressed about Vidal because Vidal had a different style and the way he played, to my humble opinion, conflict with the base player and the drum, so that's why he got impressed with Chano Pozo; because Chano Pozo was so smart that as soon that he hear the bass drummer, he played between both people.
He never conflict with the bass player and the conga player. He never had problem. He was a bright, a very bright person.
